Grounded Synthetic Intelligence Proposed as Foundational Infrastructure for Regulated Artificial Intelligence

In a position paper published in the International Journal of Computational Intelligence Systems, researchers argue that synthetic data should be recognized as foundational infrastructure for computational intelligence operating under severe data constraints. The authors introduce the concept of Grounded Synthetic Intelligence, a framework in which synthetic data functions as a scalable extension of real data while remaining anchored to authentic observations through hybrid training and validation strategies.

The authors explain that artificial intelligence is entering a post-data era where access to sensitive data, rather than its availability, has become the primary constraint on technological progress. Stringent regulatory frameworks, privacy protections, and governance requirements increasingly limit the direct utilization of real-world datasets, creating substantial barriers in critical domains such as digital health and personalized human-centric systems.

Rather than treating synthetic data as an outright replacement for real-world measurements, the Grounded Synthetic Intelligence paradigm emphasizes disciplined integration with authentic records. The framework relies on structured hybrid training and validation routines, emphasizing rigorous evaluation and governance-aware deployment to ensure that machine learning systems maintain both practical analytical utility and high trustworthiness in real-world deployments.

To examine how these principles operate in practice, the authors review empirical insights from behavioral and health data workflows. These workflows illustrate that synthetic data augmentation can successfully improve model learning and algorithmic performance in scenarios where available real-world datasets are either strictly restricted in volume or subject to heightened confidentiality constraints.

At the same time, the paper highlights significant vulnerabilities associated with using synthetic datasets in isolation from genuine observations.

The authors identify several key challenges that currently impede the broader adoption of synthetic data in computational intelligence. These unresolved issues include navigating complex fidelity–utility tradeoffs, resolving domain dependence across varied real-world applications, and addressing the persistent lack of standardized evaluation protocols for evaluating and validating synthetic datasets prior to operational deployment.

To resolve these core obstacles, the position paper outlines critical future research directions for the field. The researchers emphasize the necessity of advancing trustworthy generation techniques, developing domain-aware modeling approaches, and establishing robust integration mechanisms specifically tailored for personalized artificial intelligence architectures operating in sensitive environments.

By reframing synthetic data as an enabling infrastructure rather than a mere convenience technique, the researchers aim to guide the future design of artificial intelligence systems in increasingly regulated environments. The authors conclude that adopting this grounded paradigm will support the development of secure, privacy-preserving, and clinically useful tools across sensitive domains.

Subject of Research: Grounded synthetic data infrastructure for privacy-preserving artificial intelligence

Article Title: Beyond Real Data: Grounded Synthetic Intelligence for Trustworthy and Personalised AI

Article References: Kamal, R., Liaquat, M., Cleland, I., Nugent, C., & Khan, N. (2026). Beyond Real Data: Grounded Synthetic Intelligence for Trustworthy and Personalised AI. International Journal of Computational Intelligence Systems. https://doi.org/10.1007/s44196-026-01658-5
